issues.description: The problem statement specifies a SealSaloon constructor that takes a String (the saloon name) and implies a corresponding name/identification field initialized by that constructor. However, the provided solution's SealSaloon class only has a no-argument constructor (SealSaloon()) and does not declare or initialize any saloon name field. The template's example Main also instantiates SealSaloon with a no-arg constructor, which conflicts with the textual specification. This mismatch will confuse students about the required constructor signature and whether a name field must be implemented.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification and code consistent. Either: (A) Update the problem statement to allow a no-argument SealSaloon() constructor (and remove the requirement to pass a saloon name), or (B) modify the solution/template to implement the required constructor SealSaloon(String name) and add a corresponding private final String name field (with a getter). Ensure example usage in Main and any documentation matches the chosen constructor signature.
